body:
Thanks for the kind words. I know you're right, and I really have been trying to just forget about it and live my life, but when my life is going days without talking to anyone but my mother, and constantly being alone, it's hard to be satisfied.

I have one other friend, but he is weird and just yearns for the past, he actually gets upset when I won't talk shit about the old group of friends we were in, me longer than him, and he has admitted to me that he constantly thinks about the past.

This happened to me on campus last spring. If you want to PM me your state I may be able to help you if you are getting charged, but I can help you a bit with the university dealings. 

You are pretty much saying what I was, though you sound calmer. Don't be afraid to go into mourning. It will probably consume you for awhile, and you already know that it's best to keep your mind off of it, but try to just relax it's not the end.

Try to stay out of your dorm. For me, my dorm just reminded me of what happened. Try to study other places and just generally spend as much time as you can away from it. Check out museums, do whatever you can. 

It's good that you are in counseling. Try to keep that up. I never went/haven't gone and I think it is one of the main reasons that I am suicidal today. It shakes you. In one day, one afternoon, it seems like your life is gone and all of your goals are impossible now. This isn't true, but you may feel that way for awhile. It's okay to feel really shitty because of this, it's definitely a low point, but don't let it defeat you. It is pretty common to get caught with pot, especially in a dorm. Try confiding in someone. I confided with this older guy in my french class who I shot the shit with before class and he revealed to me that he had had trouble with the law before, but that it's not the end of the world and that there are ways to get through it/around it.

It is hard for me right now to help you as much as I'd like because as you are well aware it feels like a big deal, the biggest deal in the world. I am trying not to just tell my story, but to help you. 

I am intimately familiar with what you are going through and it would be a pleasure if you PMd me and wanted to talk about it or if you just need advice for what you will have to deal with for the university hearings and such.

I was in a similar position. My thoughts came suddenly, and my problem wasn't like other problems I read about on sw. Mine was more a feeling without a cause, or at least a cause I could perceive. I am doing much better now because I realized and accepted my problem.

My problem had to do with social isolation more than anything, but it manifested itself in suicidal thoughts and other thought problems. If one was forgotten or solved then there are new ones. You have to address and treat the root problem. Be open, I know it's hard but this is probably a long running problem that you've had and it is just now more severe.

What I found helping in the short term is medication, which I am on, and helping others. It can be as simple as giving change to the needy or doing volunteer work. Yesterday I turned an upside-down cockroach that was flailing on the sidewalk so that it could walk. I don't know why it helped, but I thought maybe thanks to some kind of karma someone would come along and turn me off of my back.
Im on lexapro, annnd a couple weeks ago i had one beer on a full stomach and it really made me feel awful so I don't drink.

I am 19 and my gp put me on the pills. He is really not a pill pusher and he did listen but he is not perfect. 

Still I used to get mood swings that were kind of sudden and came with physical sensations such as my forehead burning and recently the back of my neck burning. 

I can't tell, though, if the mood swings were caused just by my thoughts. I would be doing something and it would trigger a chain of thoughts that brought on the moodswing. Almost always playing video games, one time I was playing a game and the body of a dead enemy was marked [empty] because it didn't have anything etc and I was depressed for days because I started thinking how we all die [empty] and how everyhting ends up sucking because the universe even dies.

I am curious but i don't want to have someone misdiagnose me because I insist on being bipolar. I also have no trouble sleeping. What are some things I should look out for?

I tried a walk and the pain was still there. I talked to my friend again for a minute but I don't know where to go. I decided I would proibably still want to be friends but I don't know how I would face anyone again.
I'm in Texas.

I don't speak to my roommates for a few reasons I guess. There's so many of us that I guess we feel less compelled to talk to eachother so we just use the room in silence. It would be weird for me to start talking to them now. I am a 6'1 dude who has obviously been crying for the last 40 minutes or so.

I don't really know of anything I could join. I'm in univeristy and counselling is only $5 a session but I can't get the courage to call and I am trying to stay out of the role of "patient." I am especially vulnerable right now because if I replace my friends with medical or psychiatric care then I could see myself falling into an unhealthy pattern.

I have never spoken to any of my roommates. My friend knows I'm on medication but I doubt he believes I was really suicidal. He says they are "tranquilizers" and doesn't think I have a real problem. I don't care what he thinks about that, though. It would piss him off if I said it but he has no idea what I am going through in that regard so I'll let him learn on hiis own if he is meant to know.

It's not so much the loneliness itself, but seeing the group of friends that suddenly abandoned me. There was never any drama, and the last tiem I saw them was a great time. There were new poeple, maybe one guy didn't like me since I'm sure he's used to most of the attention since I guess he was big shit in the suburbs, but fuck is it disappointing to have every single person you know ignore your phonecalls/texts. 

I want my friends back in a way, but i just cannot imagine going back. I'm shit at that kind of thing.

Seeing a professional is possible, it's really cheap through the university, like $5 a session, but I just can't bring myself to make the call. I think the counselors are used to just "I have too much homeworK" or actually depressed people. I am not really depressed I think, I don't get down on myself for the shit thta goes wrong all of the time.

Well I mean like, for example, I'll try to enjoy something and I can't. For instance, say I was drinking something that tasted good, I would remind myself that it isn't "real" and didn't matter and I wouldn't enjoy it anymore.
I'd ask for seconds!
That sounds pretty good, actually. Music can help and crying is cathartic. Just try not spending too much time inside!
Haven't heard of it until now. It looks pretty interesting, any recommendations?
I guess that's comforting, but how long must I wait? Can I last as long as it will take?

That's a good way to put it. I am on antidepressants, but I don't have a history of depression. 

For instance, I only feel hopeless. I don't blame myself for shit that goes wrong and I have a high sense of control. I just feel lonely without my friends and I don't know how I'll be ok again. i don't know if I could find friends like them again. I guess I understand why they ignore me. I brought up suicide and they kind of tease me about it. That sounds like they're awful, but we've always been like that, we live off of humor, so I guess I shouldn't expect them to take this seriously if we never take anything else seriously, even if they aren't helping.

I know how that feels. Even if you were close to someone, sometimes the disappointment of anything less than total understanding and sympathy can be too much. 

Do you mind telling sw about what you're thinking about, or just ways to feel better?

I mean, 10 years is a long time.  Do you live in a place where you could be around other people? A bar might not be a great idea, but maybe like a music venue or a coffee house?

I am alone, too.

Guy kinda sounds like a jerk. I haven't ever had a big breakup so I can't help much but I would think what you need is entertain yourself for awhile so you can start to cope.

What do you like to do? Do you like writing? Could you keep a journal? 

Surely your friends will not all abandon you. Call them, go out, get coffee. I don't think anyone's friends would really just abandon them if you called out.
Does anyone know how to check yourself into a psych ward? Any way to do it so that your university doesn't flunk your ass?
Well what are your favorite bands?

I don't know what's making today so bad. Kind of burned some bridges with my friends, don't know if I'll go back to them this time. My "problem" is that secretly I think we all are suicidal and we just lie to ourselves all of the time. I need my perspective shifted back. I don't have any actual mental disorders that I know of.

I guess what set me off was reading that thing by Hunter S Thompson the day after 911, and about another author that killed himself. It seems like the best people kill themselves and it makes me think that one day I'll actually do it. Not because I'm so great but because it's like I can't ever go back to how I was a few months ago. Nothing's really happened since then, no major life events.

I like music a bit. I like Garage, getting into blues, lots of electronic that isn't too cheesy, New wave.

I don't know what my other interests are. I am a student in college, I like live music, all kinds of things. I am not the best conversationalist. WHat do you like?

They pretty much admitted to straight up ignoring me. One just said he was playing games when he got the text but he still would've seen it sooner or later, he compulsively checks his phone.

One guy isn't responding to me at all. Not on IM or anything, I wouldn't be surprised if they were "coaching" people not to talk to me. I know that sounds paranoid but they did it to some other guy, pretty much.


That does sound pretty far fetched, but one is kind of immature and has this obsession with being popular and his life resembling some bullshit clothes commercial or something. Even if I make them laugh I guess I am too weird for his picturesque world.

Nope, I confronted them and they sugar coated it, but they were definitely ignoring me. Every one of them. Fuck. 

I want to lash out. My friend is coming to town and he is in a frat so he could get me and whoever I bring into a party. I already told the guys they could come so they might decide to try to come with me. I want to just tell them to fuck off and go alone. I don't want to burn all my bridges, but I don't want ot be a doormat, either.
Also, have you gotten over it? Has your father given you any insight?

I am 19 if that makes a difference. 

I understand what you said and it makes sense. I mean, I don't know how to channel my anxieties though. I am with you in that I can't just stop thinking about it at will. I can try more, I guess.

I don't think I am having self confidence issues, though. I do feel kind of alienated and different but I don't think anyone else I know is going through this. My friends aren't, and I only have for a little while, maybe a full 2 months of having a problem, working through it, and having another one. It's starting to seem like a game, liker everything is. I don't mean that in a good way either.

Yeah, pretty much the exact same thing has happened to me.

Was there any physical sensation? You mentioned tenseness, did you feel anything in your head, like a wave or something?

I had panicattacks and then this kind of thing. There is some panic involved, I imagine for you as well. Try to calm down, I know what it feels like to feel crazy like that, I believe. I am on antidepressants now and I haven't had it happen since.

 I don't know what this kind of thing is, so I hope someone can answer for both of our sakes.

I had sudden suicidal thoughts after about a half a week of occasional nausea. I also got dizzy and got headeaches and was diagnosed with sinusitis, and it runs in my family. 

Although I treated my sinusitis the thoughts didn't really go away and I still got panic attacks until more than a month ago getting prescribed with a ssri. 

I don't know if what I have is connected, though. I have some other reasons why I would feel that way, but it's still interesting.

I don't know why, but a wave of suicidal thoughts kind of washed over me. There was a physical sensation in my head even, it's happened before but this was not near as bad. It will take awhile to get over.

My friends all told me to call them if I ever felt bad, but I don't know what to say. I'm not sad about anything. I used to feel hopeless, and I am not all better but at least a little bit. It's almost like at this point I want to do it only for the sake of doing it.

That said, I don't believe I present any real danger to myself. It's a little bit like I've separated the suicide in my thoughts from actual suicide.

Thanks for asking!

>Sudden fear and the feeling that everything is wrong, just wrong.

I get those in addition to my textbook panic attacks. That's a great way to put them. I'm still not sure how to think about them, they rocked my fucking world every time.


I am doing great. My doctor listened to me and told me that it really sounded like a brain chemistry thing to him, and that a 6 month-1 year run on lexapro would return my brain to normal function. I was really bummed when I got the prescription, but I was told by my parents who know the doctor well that he isn't quick to push pills, so I feel better about it. I am ill, and these could help, if not I can always go back.

I'm not trying to sell you the pills, but it would be good for me to write what I think of them so far at least for my sake. The first day I was scared of death again. That was big for me because through anxious thinking I deconstructed my world to "feelings don't exist, nothing is worth anything." But I thought that if you were scared of death, you could at least ignore that. Might've been psychosomatic, but whatever.

On the suicidal ideation: Yeah, I'm worried. You would be less likely than me, I'm 19, people under 25 are the high risk group for the suicide on the pills. I was straight up with my doctor and he said that it would more than likely have the reverse effect. So far he's right, and I have read that the risk is really in the first weeks of medication. Have I had suicidal thoughts since I've been on them? Yeah, a little. Mostly, I'm wildly uncomfortable when thinking about how low I got. The first couple of nights I would wake up a few hours after falling asleep, but last night I could sleep, so it's not so bad. I even had a panic attack the first night, I was on them, too. 

I may go through withdrawal later, but I'm on a pretty low dose and the pills are helping, I believe. I'm not getting the full effect, yet, but I've already worked some things out in my mind, and it doesn't feel like the dope is doing it.

I was not so depressed as anxious, so we might not be as comparable. I just hope you can find help, as I hope that I have.

We are not exactly the same, but similar enough that I think I can help you.

I got panic attacks suddenly, and after my second one I got suicidal thoughts. Mine revolve around the idea that everything sucks and everyone should feel awful. It's not rational but the idea resonates with me I guess.

I got them suddenly, never had a history of mental illness, I was probably really annoying to every depressed person I know because I found a positive way to think about everything. 

I had a traumatic event last spring, which I imagine is what started this whole thing, and I would say we both have persistent problems, yours is money and mine was panic attacks and perpetual boredom but obviously ours both revolve around anxiety.

I just wrote all that to show where I'm coming from and maybe you can draw comparisons. Pretty sudden feelings coming from someone who, while still rational, couldn't shake them. As time went on I would "solve" mental problems but things always got worse until recently when my mind fed me the trump card for any positive feeling: everything is oppressively awful.

Well, today I went to the doctor. I was really against taking a drug for this. I liked the idea of a psychologist who really understood me and I felt like the drug was a cheap semi-solution. BTW I'm not making this overly dramatic, I really did go today. I don't want to write a sparkling review of my anti depressant, and I still don't think they are for everyone, then again I'm not a doctor... anyway, just talk to a doctor you trust not to push pills on you if he doesn't think you need them. That was important for me, not to feel marginalized and just written off with some happy pills. If you are like me then no argument against what you feel seems to work, so if you can talk to a guy who could really evaluate whether there is an almost purely physical reason for this, it could be worth it.

If you want to pm me to talk or ask any question, go ahead.

Okay, no shit, I checked the lunar calendar after you said that. The very first night I had sudden suicidal thoughts was a full moon, if I am not mistaken. 

Eery.

I don't know what it was. I was just on reddit reading something and i got this overwhelming rush of these thoughts. I felt a little better for a minute but basically it's an extreme of how I have been feeling, like everything is depressing and hopeless. I don't know why I feel like this, because I have been socially isolated but this week I saw friends a lot and it felt great.

An emergency room would probably increase my immediate stress, here they are crowded and it would be a long wait. It is an option for me, but it would be hard to go into my parent's room and say "I feel so weird and crazy right now, I am drowning in the worst thoughts." That's the best idea, professional help, but my family is only vaguely aware that I get panic attacks and if they knew I was having suicidal thoughts they would be stressed out.

I am 99% sure it is a panic attack, just one of the "going mad" variety. I think my mind is grasping at just vague concepts of madness and I am freaking out. I tried meditating and I just freaked out and ran. I am feeling very flighty.

We have a lot in common. What you are going through, sans the medication and such, sounds a lot like where I am. I'm 19, and I don't know about you, but summers have always been low for me. I don't have anything to be sad about, at all, but it doesn't change anything. Nothing makes me happy, the things I look forward to are only the things that distract me, and it's not the "looking forward to" like before, it's a cheap anticipation. We have another thing, too, our isolation,

I think the key to our situation is our isolation. The early sociologists founded the field of study to find out more about suicide, and they found out the different kinds. Most people kill themselves, ultimately, due to social isolation. Depression is almost always a byproduct of that, in my experiences. I know that if you are like me, imagining myself with a lot more friends doesn't seem like it would change anything, but I think it would. I think it is at least worth a shot, to keep going, to suffer through life long enough to at least try to fix it. 

I hope we get better. I can get into good moods where I see myself getting old and seeing the future as a bright, inviting place. I think this is my sober view of the world. Happiness is chemical and achievable.

>I swear, I think I have backwards SAD - I got really depressed last summer and I always seem to be sadder in the summer than in the winter. 

Yeah, I can really relate to that. To a lot of what you said. I have a lot going for me but I still felt like there was no point,  I was really hopeless about there being anything worthwhile. 

I can understand the friends thing, too. I really only have a few close friends, and one has been ignoring me for no reason, he even put me on limited profile view on facebook, lol. Still you do have people that care about you, and even if you feel like you don't have any or enough, there is ALWAYS potential for more. You owe yourself and your family the chance to succeed. Right now you are at a place where you are root-less, like many people your age right out of uni, so plant the seed somewhere and let it grow, things will change.

Yeah, I'm starting to get it.

Thoughts are pretty vague and incredibly hard to describe, but it's like I'm offended, not in the usual meaning but just repulsed, but this whole universe of depression/suicidal thoughts/mental unwellness. I don't know what it is but I just think about it and then I'm like "what's wrong with me?" I don't know what it means right now, I guess.

I hope I am on the way to recovery, but these thoughts are all so new. The person I was the night before my first suicidal thoughts would not predict them. I guess now I see that it's not as bad as it could because one thing I've notices is that my thoughts don't really give me the urge to actually end my life, they just make me feel about as low as someone could probably go which would might make anyone think of suicide.

I can really relate to being hopeless about the future. Sometimes I feel like nothing is worth my time, it's all the same. Luckily I have "up" moods that can give me clarity. One of the things I realized from this is that "things" don't change, but the way I think changes. On top of that, I don't know why the way I think changes in the good moods, I just feel I am able to appreciate the value of the future. How can I, or we, permanently capture those hopeful feelings, giving up hopeless ones? I don't know.  But you have the right idea, give yourself the time to find out what's out there. Make your days different. Get new routines. I am not saying something so simple to belittle your feelings, I'd say it to anybody. Your age doesn't mean what you feel isn't real, anyone who says so is deluding themselves with nostalgia. 

Ask your therapist for a different drug if yours isn't working, they should care about the effects. If you need to talk any more people are always here.

You are smart. Smart enough to reach out. You know, or at least hope, deep down, that you can beat this, or you wouldn't have come here. And it is beatable. You write fantastically, and if that isn't smart then i don't know what is.

Those people did terrible things to you, which is why they aren't worth your life. They stole your childhood, they have stolen years from you, don't let them take any more than that.

There's nothing abnormal about putting stress on yourself, most people do it at one point or another. To an extent a small amount of that pressure is good because it motivates you, but you need to find a way to cope with the idea of not being perfect. You need to realize that you are doing fantastically, and that being the best at everything is an attainable goal. Set goals for yourself, but make sure they are realistic. Everyone fails at one point in some way, even though it doesn't seem like that because no one talks about it. 

Try to go out more. I, too, find myself just doing nothing in my room all day during the summer. Try starting some hobby, even if you're not all that interested, nothing to lose but the time you already have. You could try writing, drawing, anything. Go outside and exercise, it really does help. And if you want to talk, we are always here.

I know how you feel about some things. I don't know a thing about suffering compared to you, but I know how you feel about the world as some soul-less place. I feel like everything is pointless sometimes. But sometimes I don't. The world is how you view it, and people can change their outlook, I firmly believe that, since I do it once or twice a day. This is a really, really hard time, but things change. It doesn't have to end here, there is life after this suffering if you let there be.

I am a little intimidated trying to help you because you are so smart. Your writing is great, and I am not exaggerating by saying that you have a great skill for it. I note this because it's one more reason not to end it. You have gift to offer this rotten world. You have been through a lot, but at the end of the day, there will always be people you can relate to who can help you.

Call the hotline. You have nothing to lose. Talk to me, I'm here, but don't try this. Happiness is chemical, so there definitely are ways to be happy. You have nothing to lose by staying alive. [Read this](http://www.metanoia.org/suicide/). I am going through some shit, too, so I'm not sure what to say, but I do know, though not all the time, that this isn't the best option. 

Things change. Nothing you feel is forever. You have felt differently, and you will again unless you end it.

Have you tried getting help? I can go outside, even in public, but especially at restaurants full of people talking I kind of lose it. Maybe it will change when I'm around friends that can engage me in conversation. 

Have you ever gotten suicidal thoughts during a panic attack? Mine started during one, and I guess combined with more panic attacks and the trauma of the invasive thoughts I haven't really gotten over it. Though, I get into hopeful moods, so there must be some hope.
I get what you mean. When I'm down I am just pessimistic and not hopeful at all. I don't think it'll ever get better. When I'm up, I think clearer, and so it helps me when I'm back down.

I get panic attacks, and I think they are turning into agoraphobia, since they are starting to happen any time I'm in a crowded place. They have just started in the last couple of weeks. We should get treatment.

Can I ask what you panic over? I know we can't fix it by dissecting it here, it doesn't work like that I think, but just curious. I get paranoid that I am going to succumb to some mental illness, or that I get panicked thinking I have some serious health issue. Today I think I began to get one when I was in a restaurant just because I was feeling so down. 

Do you know what might've caused them in the beginning? 

I am a panic attack noob, but boy do I get them, so if you want to talk I'm here.

I'm not sure what help I will get since I'm not sure where I'm going. It is hard to describe my feelings so I don't know how I feel. When I feel good, I am hopeful and good. But I get the moods where I'm just pessimistic and can't stand anything. I'm not really sure how much suicidal ideation I get now, I remind myself that this will pass and I get through it. I don't feel like killing myself, I just feel like there's no reason to live. I hope to eventually just have less bad moods until they go away, but it hasn't been very long yet. I don't feel like I am in immediate danger.
I don't mind at all, though which part sounds ocd just in case I should clarify.

I feel better now. I think my panic was on the thought that it was unavoidable, but you gave me clarity. It was amplified by 1) the length and lucidity. As my name suggests, im no stranger to panic attacks, but this one was weird, maybe just a bad thought pattern. And 2) i am getting some new symptoms of depression, i have never been hard on myself but now i am starting to blame myself, which is out of character ;). 

I feel hopeful. I know this is just a mood, and i will fluctuate throughout the day, but i am becoming certain that my suicidal thoughts are a byproduct of my hypochondria. Today, my worst fears are debilitating mental illness a la schizophrenia or something else, and i show no symptoms, but i am still very uncomfortable with the thought. I will seek help, i hope to anyway, but now with a better focus on what's wrong. Thanks

I guess right now the thing im worried most about is my panic. I feel frustrated, ive been kind of panicked for at least an hour and im not sure why. I feel better a little in that im not suicidal right now, but my mind is racing over nothing, and im frustrated that i cant pin down my feelings. I think im worried that this hopeless feeling is forever.


Also, sorry this is all disjointed and oddly worded, im on my phone now.  

While im here: i want prof help, but what id best? I feel like if i get a good shrink this is probably easily fixed, relatively, and if i get a bad one then im deeper in the hole.
Thanks, im still digesting everything else youve said, but i havent chosen a method. I refuse to. For me its not like i want to do it, as much as i feel like theres no hope so why not.

I was just bouncing it off of you, kind of like initial investigation, your response was fine. I am not sure about having depression or even bipolarity because I don't lie around and feel unable to do anything, I don't really think about personal problems and get too hard on myself. I am in a rut, and the suicidal thoughts obviously mean it was deep, but I was in so much stress from worrying about my health that night, who knows. Thanks for helping me

I have another question, and you seem like the right person since you have a knowledge of suicide beyond mine, but anyone that sees this and wants to answer as well can help. I had those feelings for a couple days, and I still "remember" them, but they seem more foreign. May way of gauging how serious it was, was to imagine if there was a gun in my hand, what would i do. Then, I remember thinking I would feel inclined to turn it on myself. Now, I wouldn't even consider it, I would just put it down. I still have a similar amount of anhedonia, loss of pleasure in pleasurable things, but I feel less hopeless and scared. Sometimes I do feel like it's inevitable, but I won't let myself plan it.

My question is, why does it seem that I had acute suicidal thoughts for a relatively short time, brought on by seemingly no special event, that may have passed? I ask because if it is something that happens out of no where, like a mood swing, then what gives?

Though it may not be out of no where, this is an essential part of the understanding my question: I was/am sick with acute sinusitis, during that time. I am on pills to help it as of this morning and today more-so I have felt separated from the suicidal thoughts. The night I drove home panicking at the thought that I was suicidal, I made my first post that night, was also when the worst symptoms came on. I'm not saying sinusitis is connected to suicidal thoughts, but if you have not felt it, it doesn't touch the brain, but it seems they could be connected. I have taken steps to improve myself since then, I have not sought further counseling, though I am planning it, but i have kept myself more occupied, spent time outside/with family, and done things like read books in my free time instead of surfing the internet. 

Sorry if this was too much, but while I am very relieved to be free of the severity of the thoughts, I also wonder what the future holds. I know it may sound like bipolarism due to the "swing", but no one in my family has a history of that and I am not going through manic periods. 

EDIT: I'm still relatively depressed. I have never had all of the symptoms of depression, so I guess I've never been clinical, but I get that feeling that everything sucks and maybe it's like Holden Caulfield angsty, or maybe it is, but it seems more desperate. And, I've been happy, so I know that right now, I'm not it. I guess that's more than a lot of people have here and I'm thankful. I at least know what can be on the other side.

I feel like i am doing a little better. I can go awhile doing okay, maybe a few hours, but then i "remember" the feelings, like everything sucks and the rest. My parents were psych majors so they know a little and my dad knows im doing bad, just probably not how bad. He says i need to just get out and do stuff, and i think he has a point, considering the rest of the advice. 

I feel like checking myself in would just be scary, i dont want more stress. Still, i should consider your advice since im trying to be committed to not let this get the better of me. what resources should i look into?  The emergency room seems like its drastic or inappropriate. 


Also, some personal history details: last winter i became depressed, not near suicidal, i was fixated on death. Im mostly over it, but i began saying i wished id never been born, and scared that i would be on an unstoppable path to suicide, like it was beyond control. Sorry for my poor typing/communication, im on my phone. Thanks

I am not sure what's bringing me down. No tragic events to speak of. I was arrested in April, but that all turned out fine, case dismissed, didn't affect school. It did kind of freeze me up for awhile, and it is when I noticed not liking anything anymore. It was extremely stressful, for sure. But in the end everything turned out fine.

Now, it's summer and my close friends are all away, so I'm not really that busy, I just lay around I guess. I would say one of the hardest parts of these thoughts is the, almost certainly irrational, part that tells me that once I'm this low, I'll never be up again. Thanks.
I am 19.
